analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (head line 3) and adds a paragraph (head hunk ~920-926) on regenerating fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. That file is produced in darkbloom-platform by its prompt sidecar at an explicit revision, copied byte-for-byte, with the source revision and SHA-256 recorded in the commit. A provider prompt-rendering change (the Qwen JSON response_format thinking default) must land with regenerated vectors and pass scripts/verify-prompt-parity.sh. This is documentation only. It changes no runtime code, keys, attestation, WebSocket contract, cache storage, fan helper or authorization behavior. I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-041 or any related threat. The prefix-cache and SSD tier description in T-041 is not touched. The added guidance is mildly positive for integrity: it requires parity verification and recorded provenance for prompt vectors. The head excerpt supplied for this unit ends at line 474, so the new paragraph's exact line numbers were not visible. I relied on the patch hunk (+920-926) for it. Open questions are outside the supplied evidence: whether scripts/verify-prompt-parity.sh exists and enforces what the doc claims, and whether the Qwen response_format change is itself security-relevant. Neither can be judged from this doc-only diff.
